about: The Magníficat is Mary's canticle from the Gospel according to Saint Luke (Luke 1:46–55), sung at Roman Vespers. This edition preserves the traditional Latin text and its ten numbered biblical verses, followed separately by the Glory Be doxology.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s02.translation: And my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s03.translation: For he has regarded the lowliness of his handmaid: behold, from now on all generations will call me blessed.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s04.translation: For he who is mighty has done great things for me, and holy is his name.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s05.translation: And his mercy is from generation to generation for those who fear him.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s06.translation: He has shown strength with his arm; he has scattered the proud in the thoughts of their hearts.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s07.translation: He has brought the mighty down from their throne and exalted the lowly.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s08.translation: He has filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s09.translation: He has helped Israel, his servant, remembering his mercy.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s10.translation: As he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed forever.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s11.translation: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

s12.translation: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

w001.function: The predicate whose subject is “ánima” (w002) and object is “Dóminum” (w004).

w011.function: A substantival adjective agreeing with “Deo”: God as my Savior.

w013.function: Introduces the reason for Mary's rejoicing.

w015.function: Object of “respéxit.” Greek ταπείνωσις confirms the handmaid's low estate here, not praise of her own moral achievement.

w017.function: Relates the handmaid to God, the understood subject of “respéxit.”

w021.function: With “ex,” forms the temporal expression “from now on.”

w026.function: Subject of future “dicent”. It means generations, not nations.

w029.function: Dative of advantage: great things done to or for Mary.

w030.function: A substantival neuter plural adjective, object of “fecit.”

w031.function: The understood subject of “fecit,” characterized by “potens est.”

w035.function: Predicate to an understood “est,” agreeing with “nomen.”

w037.function: Genitive referring to God, who has done the great things.

w039.function: Subject of the clause with an understood copula “is.”

w044.function: With `a progénie`, forms the expression of mercy extending through successive generations.

w045.function: A substantival participle in the dative, naming those toward whom mercy extends.

w048.function: Object of “Fecit”: literally wrought or showed strength.

w050.function: Instrumental ablative with “in,” an image of God's powerful action.

w051.function: Relates the arm to God, the subject of “Fecit.”

w054.function: Ablative of respect or sphere: pride is located in the thought of the heart.

w056.function: The Latin singular is distributive: the heart belongs to each of the proud. Greek αὐτῶν explicitly confirms the plural referent, not God's heart.

w060.function: Ablative after “de,” the seat from which the mighty are brought down.

w063.function: A substantival adjective contrasted with the mighty.

w066.function: A substantival adjective in the ablative of content or filling.

w070.function: Predicative to “dívites”: the rich are sent away empty.

w071.function: In this biblical context it means coming to Israel's aid. Greek ἀντελάβετο confirms active help.

w073.function: Apposition to “Israël”. Greek παῖς confirms “servant,” not “boy.”

w075.function: Perfect participle of a deponent verb. Its passive form has active meaning and refers to God.

w077.function: Relates mercy to God. Unlike “sui” in s06, it does not refer to the proud.

w078.function: Connects the help and remembered mercy with God's earlier promise.

w079.function: A deponent participle with “est” (w080): passive form, active meaning.

w084.function: The biblical name used indeclinably in the dative, parallel to “sémini.”

w086.function: Dative singular. The collective noun denotes Abraham's descendants.

w098.function: Imperfect indicative with the understood subject “glória.”
